title: Joseph's dream (Matthew 1:18–25)
hook: a quiet carpenter plans to step away gently, then an angel says do not be afraid
carry: the one who says nothing and stays

segments.voice: Yesterday, the Magnificat: Mary's song, the mighty put down and the lowly lifted. Today, the man standing quietly at the edge of the story.

The child isn't his. Joseph is a carpenter, engaged to Mary, and Matthew already calls him her husband: the promise was binding. Then Mary is found to be with child. The law of his day gave him options, some of them harsh: a public accusation, a shame that would follow her for life. Matthew doesn't say what he felt. He tells us what Joseph decides, in one quiet sentence, before anything miraculous happens at all.
screen: `A CARPENTER, ENGAGED.` → `THE CHILD ISN'T HIS.` → `WHAT DOES HE DECIDE?`

segments.voice: Here's that sentence, in the Douay-Rheims Bible: "Joseph her husband, being a just man, and not willing publicly to expose her, was minded to put her away privately." Just, in Matthew's Greek, means righteous: someone who keeps God's law. And his righteousness doesn't reach for the harshest option. It looks for the gentlest. He'll end it quietly, so she isn't shamed. Then he sleeps, and an angel comes to him in a dream: "Joseph, son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife, for that which is conceived in her, is of the Holy Ghost." Fear not: in Luke's Gospel, the angel said the same to Mary. The child's name will be Jesus, which means God saves. Joseph wakes and does exactly what he was told. He takes Mary into his home. Search all four Gospels for anything Joseph says. There's nothing. Not one line. He dreams, he wakes, he acts, and he'll do it again when another dream tells him to take the family and run to Egypt. He's the one who says nothing, and stays. Catholics honor him for exactly that: patron of the whole Church, protector of families, of workers, and of a good death. His feast is March 19, and on May 1 the Church honors him as Joseph the Worker. A tradition says he died before Jesus began to preach, with Jesus and Mary beside him. The Gospels are silent on that too. Silent, faithful, and there.
screen: `A JUST MAN CHOOSES GENTLY.` · `FEAR NOT, JOSEPH.` · `HE NEVER SAYS A WORD.` · `PATRON OF THE WHOLE CHURCH.` · then, large: `THE ONE WHO SAYS NOTHING AND STAYS.`

segments.voice: Think of someone like Joseph, the one who shows up without being asked, who fixed the sink, drove you to the airport, sat in the back at every game, and never made a speech about it. See their face, and let yourself be grateful for them without saying anything, the way they never said anything. If you pray, you can pray for them.
Joseph's dream. A just man choosing gentleness, an angel saying fear not, and a husband who woke up and stayed.
Your line: the one who says nothing and stays. Day twenty-four is yours.

howItsDone: Catholics honor Saint Joseph on March 19 and as Joseph the Worker on May 1, ask his prayers for families, workers and the dying, and Catholic custom dedicates Wednesdays and the month of March to him.

chat.says: What did Joseph do when he found out Mary was expecting?
options: He chose to spare her shame quietly, then a dream told him to take her home.
He accused her in public at first, until an angel told him to stop.
He gave a long speech defending Mary, then they married right away.
chat.meaning: Being a just man, Joseph chose the gentlest path. After the angel's 'fear not,' he woke and took Mary home.
